title: English Practice Quiz 0965
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: In a professional email, the greeting should usually be ___.
options: polite and appropriate to the recipient
questions.explanation: A suitable greeting establishes a respectful tone.

questions.question: Writing an entire email in capital letters can seem ___.
questions.explanation: All-capital text is commonly interpreted as shouting.

questions.question: Before forwarding a message, you should ___.
options: check its accuracy and whether sharing is appropriate
questions.explanation: Checking accuracy and appropriateness helps prevent misinformation.

questions.question: Which phrase is a polite way to interrupt?
options: Excuse me, may I add something?
questions.explanation: This phrase requests a turn respectfully.

questions.question: A concise message is one that is ___.
questions.explanation: Concise communication uses few words while retaining the necessary meaning.

questions.question: When leaving a voicemail, include ___.
options: your name, reason for calling and a callback number
questions.explanation: These details help the recipient identify and return the call.

questions.question: If someone is speaking, active listening means ___.
questions.explanation: Active listening involves attention and relevant responses.

questions.question: Which closing is suitable for a formal email?
questions.explanation: Kind regards is a widely accepted professional closing.

questions.question: A message sent to the wrong recipient should be ___.
options: addressed promptly, following the organisation's procedure
ignored if it contains confidential details
questions.explanation: A mistaken disclosure should be handled promptly under the applicable procedure.

questions.question: When giving directions, it is helpful to use ___.
questions.explanation: Specific landmarks and ordered steps make directions easier to follow.
